blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, last-mile delivery is the single most visible interface between a company and its customer. Everything the marketing team has worked on — brand, promise, trust — is delivered or destroyed by a driver on a doorstep. A brilliant brand paired with a terrible last mile is not a long-term business; it is a slow migration toward a competitor whose last mile hurts slightly less.

Strategic leaders invest accordingly. They route last-mile decisions through customer experience, not just through cost. They own the data on failed deliveries, missed windows and driver ratings with the same seriousness as they own the P&L. They understand that a customer saved from one bad delivery is cheaper than a customer won from scratch by marketing.

The quiet truth of last mile is that it is significantly more expensive than it looks and considerably more strategic than it is usually treated. The companies that invest as if that were obvious tend, over five years, to quietly take share from those that do not.

items.q: According to the text, why is last-mile delivery so significant at senior level?
options: It is the cheapest part of the supply chain
It is fully controlled by the marketing team
It is the most visible interface between company and customer
items.why: "the single most visible interface between a company and its customer".

items.q: What does the text say strategic leaders route last-mile decisions through?
items.why: "They route last-mile decisions through customer experience, not just through cost."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A strong brand can compensate indefinitely for poor delivery.
A failed delivery can undo years of brand-building.
Last mile is more strategic than it is usually treated.
Retaining a customer is cheaper than winning a new one.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que marca brilhante + last mile ruim não é negócio de longo prazo — a marca não compensa a entrega ruim.

items.q: The phrase "a slow migration toward a competitor whose last mile hurts slightly less" suggests that…
options: price is the only reason customers switch
customers drift away gradually toward marginally better rivals
customers leave abruptly after a single failure
items.why: Inferência: "slow migration" e "slightly less" indicam saída gradual em direção a um rival apenas um pouco melhor.

items.q: What does the closing paragraph imply about companies that treat last mile as merely a cost?
options: They have no visible brand problem
They will quietly lose share to those who invest
They will gain market share over five years
They spend more on marketing than rivals
items.why: Inferência: se os que investem "take share from those that do not", os que não investem perdem participação.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando o argumento ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Let me put this as directly as I can. For years we have discussed last mile in this room as a line on the cost side, and only the cost side. I want us to move it, today, to the customer-experience side of the ledger — because that is where it actually lives.

Here is the number that should worry us. A customer we save from one bad delivery is considerably cheaper to keep than a customer marketing has to win back from scratch. And yet we scrutinise the marketing budget line by line, while failed deliveries and missed windows barely reach this table.

I am not asking for more couriers. I am asking that we own the data — driver ratings, failure rates, missed windows — with the same seriousness we bring to the P&L. Treat the doorstep as the moment the brand is either honoured or quietly broken.

The firms that already think this way are, over five years, taking share from the ones that do not. I would rather we were on the taking side of that sentence than the losing side. Give me the mandate, and I will show you the return.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where does Sophie want last mile to be discussed?
options: On the customer-experience side of the ledger
On the cost side of the ledger
items.why: "I want us to move it… to the customer-experience side of the ledger."

items.q: According to Sophie, which customer is cheaper?
options: A customer saved from one bad delivery
A customer won back from scratch by marketing
items.why: "A customer we save from one bad delivery is considerably cheaper to keep…"

items.q: What does Sophie explicitly say she is NOT asking for?
items.why: "I am not asking for more couriers. I am asking that we own the data…"

items.q: What does Sophie imply by contrasting the scrutinised marketing budget with barely-discussed failed deliveries?
options: The board misallocates its attention, ignoring a cheaper lever
items.why: Inferência: ela aponta uma incoerência — escrutinam o caro (marketing) e ignoram o barato e estratégico (last mile).

items.q: What is Sophie's overall stance toward the board?
options: Persuasive and confident, seeking a mandate
items.why: Inferência: ela argumenta com convicção e pede um mandato — "Give me the mandate, and I will show you the return."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The doorstep is the last interface between the brand and the buyer." An interface here is…
options: a point of contact between two parties
items.why: Interface = o ponto onde marca e cliente efetivamente se encontram.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Every ___ — a parcel that never arrives — chips away at the trust marketing built."
items.why: Failed delivery = entrega falhada, o pacote que não chega.

items.q: "A missed window costs more in trust than in freight." A missed window is…
options: a broken pane at the depot
a delivery that falls outside the promised time slot
items.why: Missed window = a janela de entrega prometida que não foi cumprida.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "We treat ___ as a proxy for how customers actually perceive the brand."
items.why: Driver ratings = avaliações do motorista, usadas como termômetro da percepção de marca.

items.q: "Over five years, disciplined operators take share from careless ones." To take share means to…
items.why: Take share = conquistar participação de mercado dos concorrentes.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de conselho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the last-mile investment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new delivery model city by city." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Finance pushed back on reclassifying last mile as customer experience." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Owning the failure data is what will move the needle on retention." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir uma diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The team promised improvements but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi prometido.
